conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hello, I’m Dr. Lee. I understand you came in because your dialysis fistula wasn’t working today?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, at dialysis they said no blood was flowing. My right arm fistula—just stopped working. I didn’t feel any pain or anything.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. We checked with an ultrasound, and it shows the graft is completely clotted. That’s why the blood couldn’t flow through.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Oh. Is that dangerous? I’ve had this fistula less than a year.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s serious because you need it for dialysis, but we can fix it. The interventional radiology team will do a procedure tomorrow to clear the clot and open up the blockage.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will I be able to go home after?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll see how it goes. You’ll likely stay one night, maybe two. You’ll get dialysis here while we fix the fistula.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. My wife is here—she can help translate if I don’t understand.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Thank you. We’ll make sure you both understand everything. For now, you need to stay NPO—nothing to eat or drink—after midnight in case of the procedure.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Nothing to eat? Even water?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: No food or drink, not even water, after midnight. It’s for your safety during the procedure.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. And my blood pressure and labs—they looked okay?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your labs are stable. Potassium is a bit high at 5.3, but not dangerous right now. Your kidney numbers are expected for someone on dialysis.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good. I’ve had high potassium before—caused heart issues.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we saw that in your history. We’ll be careful with your medications and make sure you get dialysis soon.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. The radiology team is ready to do the procedure. They’ll use a special machine to open the clot in your fistula.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will it hurt?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: They’ll give you medicine to help you relax and numb the area. You might feel some pressure, but not sharp pain.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And they’ll fix the whole thing?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: They’ll clear the clot and open up a narrowing in the vein. But they’re concerned it might narrow again, so you may need another procedure soon.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So it might happen again?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Possibly. They found a tight spot in the large vein near your chest. Even after opening it, it could close again. They’ll schedule a follow-up in the next two weeks.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, you’re back from the procedure. They successfully cleared the clot and opened the narrowed vein using balloons.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I felt some pressure, but okay. Is it fixed now?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The fistula is working again—there’s good blood flow and a strong thrill. But there’s still some narrowing, so you’ll need to go back for another check.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: When?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: They’ll call you with an appointment in the next two weeks. If it closes again, they might need to place a stent.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. And my dialysis?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ll get a full dialysis session this afternoon. After that, you can go back to your normal M-W-F schedule.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your labs after the procedure look stable. Hemoglobin is a bit low, but expected. Potassium is now 5.8—still okay since you’ll dialyze soon.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my blood sugar? I’m diabetic.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your glucose was high at 362, but that’s common in the hospital. We kept your insulin lower since you were NPO. At home, go back to your usual dose.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Should I check it at home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, check your blood sugar regularly. If it’s below 100, reduce your glargine to 7 units and call your doctor.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. What about my other meds?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ll go home on all your usual medications—amlodipine, aspirin, sevelamer, pravastatin, and the rest. We restarted your gabapentin today.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good. I was worried about that.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good news—you’re doing well. Your fistula has a strong thrill, and you’re stable. We’re clearing you to go home today.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you. When will I hear about the follow-up?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The radiology team will call you within the next two weeks to schedule the next procedure. Keep checking your fistula daily for a thrill.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. And dialysis on Monday as usual?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, resume your normal dialysis schedule. And don’t forget to monitor your blood sugar and take all your meds.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll do that. Thank you, Doctor.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Take care, and we’ll see you in follow-up if needed.
